footnote.showInPanel: Show this note in the Script Notes panel
footnote.title: Footnote and Endnote
footnote.printNotesHint: While this is off, notes stay on screen only — nothing changes in the script, the page count, or any export.
footnote.locationHint: Where notes go by default. Any note can be sent the other way from its own dropdown in the Script Notes panel; the rest follow this.
footnote.endnoteNumberingHint: Endnotes are one list at the end of the script, so there is no page to restart the numbering on.
footnote.generalNotesHint: General notes are attached to the file rather than to a line of it, so they always print at the end whatever this says.
footnote.includeInExportsHint: Applies to PDF, Word and Final Draft. Turn it off to send a clean script without changing anything on screen.
footnote.printCount_one: {{printing}} of {{count}} note is set to print.
footnote.printCount_other: {{printing}} of {{count}} notes are set to print.
footnote.printNone: No notes are set to print yet — use the Print button on a note.

page.label: Page #
page.hint: The number printed on this page

pages.label: Total Pages
pages.hint: The number on the last page

headerFooter.title: Header & Footer
headerFooter.numberingHint: The number printed on the first script page. The title page is never numbered and never counted. Raise this when the opening sheet should read as a later page — a synopsis on the first sheet, for instance, makes the script start at 2.

revisions.title: Revision Settings
revisions.markEmpty: The revision mark cannot be empty.
revisions.markHelp: Printed in the right margin beside every revised line. Final Draft and most productions use {{mark}}.
revisions.perRevisionHelp: Leave a revision blank to use the mark above. A line carrying more than one revision shows the latest one’s mark.
revisions.colorPages: Print revised pages on colored paper
revisions.colorPagesHelp: PDF and Print tint each revised page in its latest revision’s color, so it can be told apart without colored stock.

moresContds.title: Mores & Continueds
moresContds.autoContdHelp: Adds the marker when a character speaks again after an action line within the same scene. It is never added across a scene heading.
moresContds.pageBreak: Show {{more}} / {{contd}} when dialogue breaks across pages
moresContds.pageBreakHelp: When a single speech splits over a page break, shows {{more}} at the bottom of the page and the character name with {{contd}} at the top of the next.

fonts.title: Fonts
fonts.intro: OpenDraft comes with a full library of screenplay, serif, sans-serif, monospaced and display fonts. Add your own TrueType (.ttf) or OpenType (.otf) files here to use them anywhere in a script, and in exported PDFs.
fonts.fileHint: {{extensions}}, up to {{size}} MB each. Add each weight as its own file to get real bold and italic.
fonts.deviceCount_one: {{count}} font installed on this device are available in the picker.
fonts.deviceCount_other: {{count}} fonts installed on this device are available in the picker.
fonts.deviceHint: Fonts installed on this device can be used as well as the built-in library.
fonts.namedHelp: This platform will not list its fonts, so OpenDraft looks for the ones it knows about. If you have another font installed — through a font app or a profile — type its name and it will be added if this device can render it.
fonts.note: A script records the name of the font it was written in, so it keeps that choice when you open it on another device. Where the font isn't installed there, OpenDraft substitutes the closest match of the same kind — a typewriter face for a typewriter face, a serif for a serif — and the original name is restored as soon as the script is opened somewhere the font exists.

titlePage.includeInOutputHelp: Takes effect straight away and is remembered on this device. Final Draft, Fountain and Fade In files always carry the title page.
